title: Cursor pagination with a navigable envelope and enforced limits
iWant: stable cursors, next and prev links, and predictable page sizes on every collection
soThat: I can traverse any collection completely and efficiently without skipped or duplicated items

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every collection endpoint accepts ?cursor= and ?limit= and responds with the declared pagination envelope carrying items, next, and prev.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a page is requested with cursor and limit
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response conforms to the pagination envelope with items, next, and prev fields

acceptanceCriteria.description: next is null on the last page and prev is null on the first; following next repeatedly from the first page visits every item exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a collection with a known item set spanning multiple pages
acceptanceCriteria.when: the collection is walked via next from the first page
acceptanceCriteria.then: every item appears exactly once and the final page's next is null

acceptanceCriteria.description: Cursors are opaque: they carry no client-decodable positional semantics the client is invited to construct, and a tampered cursor is rejected with 400 and a problem-details body.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 400 with the declared error envelope rather than best-effort interpretation

acceptanceCriteria.description: Pagination is write-stable: items present in the collection for the whole traversal are neither skipped nor duplicated when concurrent inserts and deletes occur mid-walk.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a traversal in progress while other clients insert and delete items
acceptanceCriteria.then: every item that existed throughout appears exactly once

acceptanceCriteria.description: The declared maximum limit is enforced: a request exceeding it receives 400 with a problem-details body naming the maximum, and a request without a limit receives the declared default page size.
acceptanceCriteria.given: requests with an oversized limit and with no limit
acceptanceCriteria.then: the oversized request receives 400 naming the maximum; the limitless request returns the default page size

acceptanceCriteria.description: Total counts are off by default and returned only when explicitly requested via the documented parameter, so the expensive count is never paid unknowingly.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a collection request without the count parameter and one with it
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the explicit request carries the total, per the envelope's documented count field
